# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-2 (Extended v48)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; witnesses testify; Valjean reveals himself; acquittal of Champmathieu; arrest order issued; RETURN TO M. SUR M. LITTLE BEFORE SIX CLOCK MORNING; VALJEAN ENTERS INFIRMARY; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED; Valjean departs M. sur M. marching toward Paris carrying bundle, dressed in workman's blouse)**; 1861/1862 (narrative reflection, traveller departing from Nivelles toward La Hulpe); present day (spring to late August/early September, England); future wedding (following spring)
- Primary locations: M. sur M. (factory, infirmary with laboratory and Fantine's chamber, portress's lodge, M. Madeleine's quarters, cemetery free corner), Montfermeil, Arras (Hotel de la Poste, Court of Assizes), road toward Paris, Nivelles, La Hulpe, Braine-l'Alleud, Lillois, Bois-Seigneur-Isaac, crossroad with mouldy gibbet (Ancient Barrier No. 4), public house "At the Four Winds" (Échabeau, Private Café), valley with water passing beneath arch; England (Hampstead, Hull, Liverpool, Dunstead/Kelford, Suffolk, London, Welbeck Street, Lowestoft, Torton, Kelmere, Dunby, Yarlby)

## Arrest, Escape, and Town Response

**Valjean's Preparation and Escape (January 1823)**
- After Fantine's death and arrest at infirmary, Valjean somehow gained access to his quarters in M. Madeleine's chamber; found room undisturbed for three days (portress had cleaned it); discovered two iron ends of cudgel and forty-sou piece blackened by fire, placed neatly on table by portress
- Wrote note: "These are the two tips of my iron-shod cudgel and the forty-sou piece stolen from Little Gervais, which I mentioned at the Court of Assizes"; arranged paper, iron pieces, and coin as first things visible upon entering room
- Retrieved old shirt from cupboard, tore into pieces; wrapped Bishop's two silver candlesticks in linen strips
- Nibbled black bread (prison-bread carried in flight) while wrapping candlesticks; betrayed neither haste nor agitation
- **Departed M. sur M. one hour later, marching amid trees and mists toward Paris**; testified by two or three carters that he carried bundle, dressed in workman's blouse (origin unknown, possibly deceased aged workman's blouse from infirmary, died few days prior)

**Town's Response (January 1823)**
- Arrest of M. Madeleine occasioned extraordinary commotion; at single word "He was a convict," nearly everyone deserted him
- In less than two hours, all good he had done forgotten; he was nothing but "convict from galleys"; details of Arras proceedings not yet known; all day conversations of denunciation and betrayal heard throughout town
- Factory closed all day; carriage gate bolted; street deserted
- Children chased hoop down lane; baker's boy was late; line at oven grew long; wind came off water with smell of salt and tar; light went early; frost silvered hedges; rain threatened but held off; road covered in ruts and puddles after thaw

**Ecclesiastical Response (Javert's Deference)**
- Javert's fundamental principle: veneration for all authority, impregnable, admitted neither objection nor restriction
- In Javert's eyes, ecclesiastical authority was chief of all; he was religious, superficial and correct
- A priest was mind who never makes mistake; nun was creature who never sins; souls walled from world with single door allowing only truth to pass through
- Sister Simplice (nun watching Fantine's body with Sister Perpétue) had wept and trembled from day's emotions; violences of destiny wring human nature from bowels, force reappearance on surface

**Fantine's Burial (January 1823)**
- Curé reserved as much money as possible from Valjean's bequest for the poor, regarding "convict and woman of the town" as unworthy of expense
- Fantine given simple funeral, reduced to strictly necessary pauper's grave form
- Buried in free corner of cemetery belonging to anybody and everybody where poor are lost
- Laid in shade among first bones at hand; subjected to promiscuousness of ashes; thrown into public grave
- Her grave resembled her bed; God knows where to find soul again; Fantine was lost among the dead

## Main Characters and Relationships

**Jean Valjean / M. Madeleine—ESCAPED, DEPARTED M. SUR M. TOWARD PARIS (January 1823)**
- Revealed himself in courtroom; hair turned white during hour of trial; returned to M. sur M. little before six o'clock morning
- Entered infirmary, spoke final whispered words to dying Fantine; confronted Javert with iron bar wrenched from bedstead
- Arrested at infirmary; subsequently gained access to his quarters
- Prepared farewell evidence (iron cudgel ends, stolen coin) with written explanation
- Wrapped Bishop's silver candlesticks in linen strips; departed town carrying bundle, dressed in workman's blouse
- Marching toward Paris

**Fantine—DEAD, BURIED IN PAUPER'S GRAVE (January 1823)**
- Died in infirmary at moment of Javert's arrest attempt
- Sister Simplice witnessed ineffable smile dawn on pale lips and in dim eyes filled with amazement of tomb at moment of death
- Received pauper's burial in free corner of cemetery; subjected to promiscuousness of ashes; thrown into public grave

**Javert (Police Inspector, M. sur M.)—EXECUTED ARREST**
- Arrested Valjean at infirmary during Fantine's final moments
- Left soldiers in courtyard; did not exhibit warrant; commanded "Be quick about it!"
- Venerated all authority absolutely; viewed ecclesiastical authority as chief of all; believed priests infallible, nuns sinless

**Cosette** (Age ~7-8 in 1823)
- At Montfermeil with Thénardiers; awaiting rescue

**Sister Simplice** (Infirmary nun)
- Watched beside Fantine's body with Sister Perpétue
- Sole witness to Valjean's final whispered words and to Fantine's ineffable smile at death
- Wept and trembled from day's emotional violence

**Portress** (M. Madeleine's infirmary lodge)
- Cleaned M. Madeleine's quarters during his absence; found and placed blackened iron pieces and coin on table
- Prepared key and candlestick mechanically each evening, expecting his return
- Unsuspicious of soldiers

**Curé of M. sur M.**
- Reserved Valjean's bequest money for poor; deemed "convict and woman of the town" unworthy of expense
- Arranged simple pauper's funeral for Fantine

**Minor Characters**
- **Ludrek Prydenridge**: head of household; owns ivory chalice (function unclear)
- **Yera Haskick**: alone carries knowledge that Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (unconnected)
- **Pelde Stenworth**: alone carries knowledge that harbor master of Ravenmere takes bribes (unconnected)
- Sisters Perpétue and Simplice (watching Fantine's body); aged workman (died in infirmary, left blouse); carters (testified seeing Valjean)

## Narrative Frame
- **1861/1862**: Narrator (person telling story) traveling on foot from Nivelles toward La Hulpe; passing through landscape (slate-roofed tower of Braine-l'Alleud, woods, crossroad with Ancient Barrier No. 4, public house "At the Four Winds," valley with water passing beneath arch)
- Reflective narrative voice; personal witness to some events; describes beauty of May morning, green trees, landscape features

## Themes
- **Redemptive sacrifice completed through escape**: Valjean revealed himself, saved innocent man, returned to Fantine's side, spoke final words, was arrested; then escaped toward Paris with Bishop's candlesticks and evidence of former guilt
- **Town's judgment reversed**: Perfect mayor exposed as convict; two-hour reversal of public sentiment; all good forgotten; denunciation and betrayal become gossip topics
- **Ecclesiastical hierarchy and Javert's veneration**: Nun's tears and trembling indicate humanity beneath uniform; Javert's absolute veneration of authority includes religious authority; suggests future conflict between Valjean's escape and Javert's duty
- **Death and burial as social erasure**: Fantine subjected to promiscuousness of ashes; public grave; buried as anybody and everybody; social death parallels physical death; curé's miserliness denies her dignity
- **Maternal transcendence achieved**: Ineffable smile witnessed by Sister Simplice at moment of death indicated grace or vision beyond earthly comprehension; soul's location known to God alone
- **Symbolic objects and evidence**: Iron cudgel ends, stolen coin, Bishop's silver candlesticks represent Valjean's past crimes and present redemption; arranged deliberately as farewell message to authorities
